newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian family pleads for alleged coup plotter.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian family pleads for alleged coup plotter.

text.p: The family of Nigerian democracy activist Beko Ransome-Kuti called on Monday for his release, two years after the military government jailed him for taking part in an alleged coup plot.

"My father is physically all right, although he has a fragile frame. He is in solitary confinement and he does not have access to lawyers," his daughter Nike Ransome-Kuti told a news conference in Lagos attended by foreign diplomats.
Ransome-Kuti, a medical doctor, is serving a 15 year sentence for allegedly taking part in a plot to overthrow military ruler General Sani Abacha in March 1995.
Former head of state retired General Olusegun Obasanjo and over 40 others are also serving jail sentences related to the plot.
Ambassadors from the United States and South Africa, both of which have been severely critical of Nigeria, were among the audience at Monday's news conference.

"I'm happy to be here because of my great respect for Beko Ransome-Kuti. The people of the United States and myself are greatly concerned about his state," U.S. Ambassador Walter Carrington told reporters.

Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, has been shunned by Western nations for holding dozens of political prisoners, including the presumed winner of annulled 1993 elections, millionaire businessman Moshood Abiola.
Critics both inside and outside Nigeria are unsure about the sincerity of Abacha's promise to restore civilian rule next year.
